name.text: 01 Question: Architecture of Four-Line Leipzig Glossing

questiontext.text: <p>In linguistic and philological scholarship, what are the four standard tiers of an Interlinear Glossed Text (IGT) adhering to the Leipzig Glossing Rules?</p>

answer.text: <p>Tier 1: Original source text; Tier 2: Morphological segmentation; Tier 3: Morpheme-by-morpheme grammatical gloss; Tier 4: Free idiomatic translation.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Correct. The Leipzig standard establishes these four vertical tiers to represent text from raw surface form down to morphemic analysis and free translation.</p>

answer.text: <p>Tier 1: Latin; Tier 2: French; Tier 3: German; Tier 4: English.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. The tiers represent linguistic analytical layers of a single text, not four arbitrary European languages.</p>

answer.text: <p>Tier 1: Shelfmark; Tier 2: Scribe; Tier 3: Date; Tier 4: Provenance.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. These are codicological cataloguing metadata fields, not interlinear glossing tiers.</p>

answer.text: <p>Tier 1: Author; Tier 2: Publisher; Tier 3: ISBN; Tier 4: Price.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. These are bibliographic publication metadata fields.</p>

questiontext.text: <p>According to Rule 2 of the Leipzig Glossing Rules, what is the crucial distinction between a hyphen (`-`) and a period (`.`) in the grammatical gloss line?</p>

answer.text: <p>A hyphen indicates a distinct morpheme boundary clearly segmented in the text above, while a period connects multiple grammatical meanings expressed by a single indivisible morpheme (portmanteau).</p>

feedback.text: <p>Correct. Hyphens align with physical morpheme cuts, whereas periods separate multiple category labels (e.g. '1SG.PST') that correspond to a single fused segment.</p>

answer.text: <p>A hyphen indicates an error by the scribe, while a period indicates a word that should be deleted.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Both marks are analytical tools for linguistic glossing, not scribal defect indicators.</p>

answer.text: <p>A hyphen is used only for nouns, while a period is used only for verbs.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Leipzig punctuation applies universally across all grammatical parts of speech.</p>

answer.text: <p>Hyphens are forbidden in digital editions because XML parsers cannot process them.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. XML handles standard ASCII hyphens without issue.</p>

questiontext.text: <p>How does TEI P5 represent alignment between source and target text segments without physically mingling their XML trees?</p>

answer.text: <p>Using stand-off annotation with `<linkGrp>` containing `<link target="#srcID #tgtID"/>` elements that pair IDs defined in separate `<text>` bodies.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Correct. Stand-off markup keeps each language's text hierarchy clean and autonomous, linking them via ID reference pairs inside <linkGrp>.</p>

answer.text: <p>By pasting the English translation directly into the `<author>` tag of the `<teiHeader>`.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. <author> records the author of the work, not parallel translations.</p>

answer.text: <p>By converting both documents into a single unformatted plain text file with no XML tags.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Unformatted text destroys structural alignment and XML validity.</p>

answer.text: <p>By writing both languages alternately, word by word, inside a single `<p>` tag.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Interleaving words inside a single paragraph corrupts the syntax and parsing of both languages.</p>

name.text: 04 Question: Operational Heuristic of Gale-Church Alignment

questiontext.text: <p>On what foundational heuristic does the classical Gale-Church sentence alignment algorithm operate?</p>

answer.text: <p>Sentence length correlation: across translated texts, corresponding sentences tend to have closely correlated lengths measured in character counts.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Correct. Gale and Church proved that sentence length correlation alone enables robust, language-independent dynamic programming alignment without needing bilingual lexicons.</p>

answer.text: <p>Alphabetical sorting: all sentences are sorted alphabetically from A to Z before pairing.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Sorting alphabetically destroys narrative order and textual alignment.</p>

answer.text: <p>Rhyme scheme: sentences are aligned based on whether their final syllables rhyme in both languages.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. The algorithm evaluates character count probabilities, not poetic rhyme.</p>

answer.text: <p>Parchment moisture: sentences are aligned based on the relative humidity of the manuscript room.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Physical conservation parameters have no bearing on computational text alignment.</p>

name.text: 05 Question: Statistical Word Alignment with fast_align

questiontext.text: <p>How do statistical word alignment tools like IBM Models and `fast_align` calculate word-level correspondences in parallel corpora?</p>

answer.text: <p>They use Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithms and log-linear models to find the probability that a word in the source sentence generates a specific word in the target sentence across large corpora.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Correct. Statistical aligners optimize lexical translation probabilities and positional distortion parameters using EM over sentence-aligned bitexts.</p>

answer.text: <p>They assign words randomly until the user stops the script.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Statistical alignment is a principled mathematical optimization process.</p>

answer.text: <p>They look up every word in Google Translate via an active internet browser connection.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. fast_align is a standalone mathematical model that trains directly on the input corpus.</p>

answer.text: <p>They require the user to manually type every single pairing before running.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. The purpose of statistical alignment is to automate lexical pairing across massive text collections.</p>

questiontext.text: <p>Why is word-for-word (1-to-1) alignment often impossible when translating ancient or highly inflected languages into modern English?</p>

answer.text: <p>Typological asymmetry (non-isomorphism): a single synthetic inflected word often corresponds to a multi-word analytic phrase in English (1-to-many), or an idiomatic phrase collapses into one word (many-to-1).</p>

feedback.text: <p>Correct. Languages differ in morphological synthesis; synthetic and polysynthetic words express concepts that analytic languages require auxiliary verbs and prepositions to convey.</p>

answer.text: <p>Because English grammar forbids sentences from having more than four words.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. English sentences can have arbitrary grammatical length.</p>

answer.text: <p>Because ancient manuscripts never contained verbs.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Historical languages contain rich, complex verbal systems.</p>

answer.text: <p>Because digital text editors automatically delete translation words that exceed eight letters.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Software imposes no such restriction.</p>

name.text: 07 Question: Role of Ugarit and Alpheios in Historical Alignment

questiontext.text: <p>What capability do specialized platforms like Ugarit and the Alpheios Alignment Editor offer for scholarly historical editing?</p>

answer.text: <p>They provide web-based interactive interfaces for creating, editing, and visualizing fine-grained word-level and phrase-level alignments between historical texts and translations.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Correct. Ugarit and Alpheios specialize in classical and historical language alignment, supporting token-level linking, multi-word units, and TEI/JSON export.</p>

answer.text: <p>They automatically forge ancient manuscript provenance documents to increase sale value.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Digital humanities platforms promote academic integrity, not document forgery.</p>

answer.text: <p>They are physical microfilm cameras used in library basements.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. They are digital software web applications.</p>

answer.text: <p>They encrypt text files to make them permanently unreadable by the public.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. They produce open-access, readable parallel text representations.</p>

name.text: 08 Question: AI Failure Modes in Interlinear Glossing

questiontext.text: <p>When using an LLM to generate Leipzig glosses for an unfamiliar historical language, what is a frequent critical error?</p>

answer.text: <p>Morphological confabulation: inventing non-existent grammatical prefixes or suffixes and projecting modern English semantic categories onto ancient synthetic stems.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Correct. Without deep grounding in historical grammar, LLMs frequently hallucinate morpheme boundaries and invent grammatical category labels that do not exist in the language.</p>

answer.text: <p>Formatting text using the UTF-8 character encoding.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. UTF-8 is the global standard for digital text, not an error.</p>

answer.text: <p>Responding in less than five seconds.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Rapid computation is a technical feature, not a philological defect.</p>

answer.text: <p>Saving the output as an HTML or XML file.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Producing structured markup is standard practice.</p>

name.text: 09 Question: Translating Cultural Realia in Parallel Editions

questiontext.text: <p>How should an editor handle 'cultural realia' (untranslatable culture-specific terms, e.g. weights, legal ranks, ancient religious ceremonies) in a Leipzig glossed edition?</p>

answer.text: <p>Retain the transliterated term in the segmentation line and provide a specialized grammatical/cultural label in the gloss, supplemented by commentary notes rather than misleading generic modern equivalents.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Correct. Precise philological glossing avoids anachronistic modern substitutions by preserving the technical cultural term and explaining its specific semantic domain.</p>

answer.text: <p>Replace every unfamiliar cultural term with a modern brand name.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Anachronistic commercial substitutions destroy historical scholarship.</p>

answer.text: <p>Delete the word completely from the edition and pretend it was never written.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Editorial suppression of difficult terms violates scholarly integrity.</p>

answer.text: <p>Declare that the ancient scribe was illiterate and rewrite the entire chapter.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Scholarly editing respects the historical witness.</p>

name.text: 10 Question: Significance of Parallel Corpora for Digital Philology

questiontext.text: <p>Why is rigorously aligned parallel text invaluable for computational humanities research?</p>

answer.text: <p>It provides structured training data for historical machine translation, enables cross-lingual semantic search, and powers interactive reading environments that scaffold novice language learning.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Correct. Aligned parallel corpora are the bedrock of multilingual NLP, computational lexicography, and accessible digital pedagogy for historical languages.</p>

answer.text: <p>It allows universities to discard all historical paper manuscripts in recycling bins.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Digital representations complement, rather than replace, the physical preservation of cultural heritage.</p>

answer.text: <p>It proves that all languages throughout human history originated from Python code.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Human natural languages evolved biologically and culturally millennia before computer programming languages.</p>

answer.text: <p>It makes all historical texts exactly identical in length and vocabulary.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Parallel alignment preserves the distinctive linguistic properties of each language.</p>
